prompt: Create a finished logo concept specimen for Itsy Web, a developer tool that adds reusable layouts, partials, clean URLs, local development and simple deployment to HTML. Its audience already knows HTML and CSS. This is a logo and wordmark exploration, not a website design. Use the exact visible name “Itsy Web”, with that capitalization and spacing. Use flat, crisp, vector-friendly graphic forms in deep navy #142b43 and ice blue #a4dbff on a pale #f5f9ff ground. Landscape specimen, about 3:2. A large, beautifully balanced horizontal symbol-and-name lockup is the focal point. Include a much smaller standalone symbol and a small reversed treatment on a navy strip so small-size clarity is visible. Typography should feel quietly confident, warm and precise, with carefully drawn letterforms, optical spacing, and no tech-brand gimmicks. Show only the name as text; no slogans, labels, watermarks or mockup objects. No gradients, shadows, glossy surfaces, screenshots, coding brackets, globes, rockets, network-node diagrams or generic infinity marks. The idea is THE SLOT: header, page and footer resolve into a compact architectural mark, with the central negative space suggesting an i or the place the page fits. Make a bold, surprising silhouette with exact optical alignment and elegant proportions; it must not look like a generic hamburger menu, browser window, document icon or pile of blocks. It represents HTML's missing reusable structure, expressed in one lucid graphic gesture. Pair with sturdy, distinctive custom lettering and generous but deliberate spacing. Restrained engineering character with warmth; prioritize an ownable shape that survives favicon scale.
